name: Runzao Zhiyang capsule (Chinese herbal medicine)
short: Eczema trials: mild gut upset more common with the capsule, none serious reported (18 trials); placebo trial (240): adverse events no different, unclear in whom. With antihistamines: less drowsiness.
text: Runzao Zhiyang capsule is an oral Chinese herbal medicine, and its safety data come from trials in chronic eczema and chronic urticaria, mostly with the capsule added to other treatment. In a 2021 meta-analysis of 18 randomized trials (1,896 patients with chronic eczema), mild gastrointestinal disorders occurred more often in the capsule groups and no serious adverse effect was reported; the authors describe the included studies as of suboptimal quality. In a multicentre, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in 240 people with mild to moderate chronic eczema, the abstract reports no difference in adverse event rate between the groups after 8 weeks of follow-up, which it describes only for patients whose eczema score had fallen by more than 95%, so it is unclear which patients the comparison covers; it calls the adverse events tolerable. When the capsule was added to antihistamines, a 2025 meta-analysis of 32 studies (3,071 participants with chronic eczema) found less drowsiness (risk ratio 0.50) and no significant difference in headache, dizziness or gastrointestinal discomfort, and a 2023 meta-analysis of 27 studies (2,703 patients with chronic urticaria) found fewer adverse events, including dizziness, fatigue, dry mouth and constipation, than with antihistamines alone, again with studies of suboptimal quality. The cited abstracts do not list the capsule's herbs. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
